name: Muiden: Entry Ticket to Muiderslot Castle
tagline: One of Europe's best-preserved medieval castles, just 30 minutes from Amsterdam — official skip-the-line entry to the castle and gardens
overview: Rising from the waters of the Vecht river just 30 minutes east of Amsterdam, Muiderslot is the Netherlands' most beautiful and best-preserved medieval castle. Built in 1285 by Count Floris V of Holland, this circular moated fortress looks exactly as a storybook castle should — complete with round towers, battlements, a drawbridge and a perfectly intact great hall. This official Rijksmuseum Muiderslot entry ticket gives you access to the full castle interior — knight's hall, dungeon, weapons room, historic kitchens — plus the castle gardens, at your own pace. Transport to Muiden from Amsterdam is not included but is straightforward: bus 320 from Amsterdam Centraal runs directly to Muiderslot in 35 minutes.
highlights: Full castle entry — knight's hall, dungeon, weapons room and historic kitchens
Access to the castle gardens and the full battlement circuit above the moat
Official Rijksmuseum Muiderslot product — no third-party markup, direct entry
Self-paced visit: stay as long as you like within opening hours
Easy to reach from Amsterdam by direct bus (35 min) — no car required

itinerary.description: Take bus 320 from Amsterdam Centraal Station directly to Muiderslot — it stops at the castle entrance. Alternatively, the EBS bus from Weesp (reachable by train from Amsterdam in 25 min) runs to Muiden village. By bicycle from Amsterdam, the route along the Gein and Vecht rivers takes approximately 1.5 hours each way and is extremely scenic. The castle car park is also accessible for drivers. Bus 320 departs roughly every 30 minutes; check 9292.nl for current schedules.

Cross the drawbridge into Muiderslot's circular courtyard — a round fortress built in 1285 by Count Floris V of Holland, who was murdered here by his own knights in 1296 in a conspiracy involving the English crown. The castle was rebuilt in its current form shortly after and has remained in near-original condition ever since. Explore the knight's hall where medieval banquets were held, the original castle kitchen, the dungeon, the weapons and armour room, and the private chambers. Then climb to the battlements for panoramic views over the Vecht river and the flat Dutch polder landscape stretching to the horizon. The castle gardens are included in the ticket.

included: Access to all public castle rooms at your own pace
excluded: Transport to Muiden from Amsterdam (bus 320 from Centraal, approx. €4 return)
Audio guide (available for hire at the castle)

faqs.question: Is transport from Amsterdam included?
faqs.answer: No — this ticket covers castle entry and the gardens only. Getting to Muiden is easy: bus 320 from Amsterdam Centraal goes directly to Muiderslot in 35 minutes (check 9292.nl for schedules, approximately €4 return). By bicycle from Amsterdam is also popular — the Vecht river route takes about 1.5 hours and is very scenic.

faqs.question: Is Muiderslot suitable for children?
faqs.answer: Very much so — the drawbridge, dungeon and battlement circuit make it one of the most child-friendly medieval castles in Europe. The self-paced entry ticket lets families move at their own speed.

faqs.question: Who was Count Floris V?
faqs.answer: Count Floris V of Holland (1254–1296) built the original Muiderslot in 1285 as a toll and control point on the Vecht river. He was one of medieval Holland's most capable rulers — known as 'der keerlen god' (the peasants' friend) for defending the rights of common people against the nobility. He was lured to Muiderslot and murdered by a group of Dutch and English knights in 1296 who opposed his policies and his alliance with France. The castle was rebuilt after his death and named after him.
